key.name: viewing-distance
key.summary: Assumed eye-to-screen viewing distance, in metres
key.description: Feeds the gaze cursor's angular sizing (make_gaze_cursor()) — the one input to that calculation that can't be read from the monitor itself. No unit in the key name and no prefix on the value — plain SI (metres), the same convention as everywhere else a persisted quantity has a unit at all. Millimetres and centimetres are purely internal/display concerns (pixel-density math, the Preferences spin row), never a second unit of storage.

key.name: traditional-viewport-scroll
key.summary: Whether arrow keys move the viewport or the content
key.description: Same distinction GNOME's own mouse/touchpad settings call "traditional" (true — arrow keys move the viewport itself, bringing content from the arrow's direction into the center) vs. "natural" (false — arrow keys instead drag the content, the opposite sign). Which one reads as "correct" is genuinely a matter of personal preference, not a bug either way — configurable in Preferences, defaulting to traditional.

key.name: last-image-folder
key.summary: Last folder used in the Open Image dialog
key.description: Empty string means "no folder remembered yet, use the file dialog's own default." Images usually live in one particular folder, so returning there instead of wherever the dialog last happened to default to saves re-navigating every time.

key.name: current-working-session
key.summary: The session (.bs) file Record/Playback currently work on
key.description: John, 2026-09-13: "en delt 'current working session'" — opening a session file in either Record or Playback sets this, and both toasts pick it up automatically the next time either is entered. Empty string means none yet — Forward/Play stay disabled until one is set.

key.name: autoload-project
key.summary: Whether the last-opened project reopens automatically at launch
key.description:
John, 2026-10-03: "Hvis det ikke er angitt på kommandolinja hvilket prosjekt som skal åpnes, så skal en gsettings-nøkkel sjekkes for om et prosjekt skal autolastes." Gates the existing last-project auto-reopen (on_activate(), main.cpp) — a command-line project argument always wins regardless of this setting, since the user asked for that one explicitly.
Default flipped to false 2026-10-04 — John: "Å gjenåpne en sesjon når andre testee er tilstede blir et problem... Det kan være aktuelt å bruke autoload når en analyserer sesjoner, men som default må den nok være av." Since autoload-session/ autoload-image both already require a project to be active before they do anything (John, 2026-10-03, "De to autoload for image og session forutsetter autoload for prosjektet"), leaving this one off by default is enough on its own to keep a facilitator's previous participant invisible at launch — turning it on is a deliberate opt-in for session analysis work, not something a fresh install exposes by accident.

key.name: autoload-session
key.summary: Whether the current working session reopens automatically at launch
key.description: John, 2026-10-03, same request as autoload-project, for the shared session dropdown's own current-working-session auto-load instead. Default flipped to false 2026-10-04, same conversation and reasoning as autoload-project's own — already effectively off by default via that key (this one requires a project to be active first), but set off here too rather than relying on that indirection alone.

key.name: autoload-image
key.summary: Whether the last-viewed image reopens automatically at launch
key.description: John, 2026-10-03: "Jeg tror bilde også skal være et flagg, og at vi skal ta vare på current image. Det gjør det enklere for brukeren" — tracks last-image (the actual path), not a fixed index into image-sequence, so it stays meaningful as that list itself is edited. Default flipped to false 2026-10-04, same reasoning as autoload-project/autoload-session's own.

key.name: last-image
key.summary: The image last shown in Interactive/Record, for autoload-image
key.description: Updated every time load_image() runs, or the display is cleared back to "no image" — independent of image-sequence membership, since load_image() itself never required the path to be a member of it — any readable file works, in or out of the prepared sequence.

key.name: microphone-initially-on
key.summary: Whether the Record toast's microphone starts on or off
key.description: John, 2026-09-13: "en toggle for Microphone initially on og initially off." Either way, the microphone icon in the Record toast can still be clicked to change it for that session — this only decides the state it starts in on entering Record.

key.name: speaker-initially-on
key.summary: Whether the Playback toast's speaker starts on or off
key.description: Playback's counterpart to microphone-initially-on (John, 2026-09-13: "Under avspilling så skal vi ha et høyttalersymbol. Dette skal ha en tilsvarende oppføring i Innstillinger") — the speaker icon can still be toggled for that session regardless of this default.

key.name: transcode-audio-to-opus
key.summary: Whether recorded WAV segments get auto-transcoded to Opus at Stop
key.description:
John, 2026-09-13: originally "delete-wav-after-encoding" (default true — encoding always happened, this only decided whether the WAV survived it too). Reworked 2026-09-24 across a few passes: first just a wording fix (encoding always happens; frame it as "we transcode to Opus," with the original going away being an implied consequence, not an announced deletion — "vi sier ikke eksplisitt at vi sletter fila"). Then John clarified the real choice isn't about the WAV's fate at all: "Det er ikke lengre et valg om å beholde WAV-fila, det er et valg om å transkode til Opus" — off means no transcoding happens at all, the WAV is just left as-is; on means every recorded segment gets transcoded to Opus the moment its capture pipeline closes (see stop_audio_track_and_encode()), and the WAV is discarded once that succeeds. A file whose encode fails always keeps its WAV regardless — discarding it then would lose the only copy of that audio — and now also surfaces a plain "couldn't transcode" notice rather than failing silently (John: "Jeg tror ikke vi skal forsøke å analysere årsaken til feilen, for det vil nok bli litt komplekst" — no diagnostics, just the fact that it happened).
Default flipped to `false` 2026-09-25 (John: "må starte som default Off") — turning it on now runs a real check (opus_encoding_available()) for whether opusenc/oggmux are actually installed, showing a dialog and reverting back to off if not, rather than silently leaving a setting on that can't actually do anything (see show_preferences()'s signal_changed(kTranscodeAudioToOpusKey) handler).

key.name: transcribe-audio
key.summary: Whether recorded speech gets auto-transcribed at Stop
key.description:
John, 2026-09-25: "Jeg tror vi skal legge på en opsjon i Innstillinger for hvorvidt talere skal transkriberes." Separate from transcode-audio-to-opus — that one is about the audio *format* (Opus vs WAV), this one is about whether maybe_transcribe_segment() runs at all. Off skips it entirely — no subprocess, no toast, no .vtt file.
Default flipped to `false` the same day, same message as transcode-audio-to-opus's own default flip ("må starte som default Off") — turning it on now runs two sequential checks (transcription_available() for the venv, then whisper_model_cached() for the fixed transcription model), each with its own dialog warning about real disk space. See show_preferences()'s transcribe_row handler.

key.name: diarize-audio
key.summary: Whether transcripts get speaker labels (diarization)
key.description: John, 2026-09-26: "Muligens må denne ha en ekstra toggle i Innstillinger. Eneste grunnen til at dette ikke slås på er at brukeren av en eller annen grunn må spare plass." — the only *principled* reason to leave it off once set up is disk space (an extra pyannote model download), but the default itself is still **false**, same as transcribe-audio/transcode-audio-to-opus above (John, same day, correcting an earlier "default true" pass: "Start med av, og la brukeren treffe plakaten når han kommer dit") — diarization needs real one-time manual setup (a HuggingFace account, license acceptance, an access token stored in GNOME Keyring) that can't happen automatically, so there's nothing to be meaningfully "on" about until the user actually does that, the same way turning it on triggers the setup poster by hand. Only takes effect when transcribe-audio is also on — diarization labels speakers within an existing transcript, it doesn't produce one on its own. See show_preferences()'s diarize_row handler and notes.md, "Diarization setup: a keyring-based HuggingFace token".

key.name: yaw-augmented-input
key.summary: Optional extra input device for horizontal panning (yaw)
key.description: Arrow keys always pan the viewport regardless of this setting (John, 2026-09-21: "Piltaster kan vel fungere uavhengig av hva som er valgt som 'augmented input method'") — this key only picks an *additional* device that works alongside them, not a replacement. One of "none" (the default — no augmented device; shown as "None available" if nothing beyond arrow keys has been validated yet), "scroll-wheel", "surface-dial" — a plain string enum, not a GSettings enum type, matching how RecordMeta's `rights` field already does free-text-with-known-values elsewhere in this app. Only input methods actually validated on real hardware are offered in the Preferences dropdown (John: "Vi fjerner de oppføringene vi ikke finner at har noe for seg"); an unrecognized value here (e.g. hand-edited) falls back to "none".

key.name: tilt-augmented-input
key.summary: Optional extra input device for vertical panning (tilt)
key.description: Arrow keys' tilt/pitch control always works regardless of this setting, same as yaw-augmented-input. One of "none" (default), "scroll-wheel" — no "surface-dial" entry here, since the Surface Dial only has a single rotation axis (yaw), not a tilt one. See yaw-augmented-input's own comment for the rest of the reasoning.

key.name: transcription-model-size
key.summary: Which Whisper model size transcribe.py loads
key.description: John, 2026-09-30: "som default skal vi bruke minste modell som får plass i GPU'en... brukeren skal imidlertid kunne be om en større modell" — faster_whisper/CTranslate2 has no automatic "pick the largest that fits" negotiation (checked directly against its own WhisperModel constructor), so this is a plain manual choice rather than anything auto-detected: "small" (default — safest fit on a constrained GPU, e.g. the 5.66GB one this project was developed against), "medium", or "large-v3". One of "small"/"medium"/"large-v3" — a plain string enum, not a GSettings enum type, same convention as yaw-augmented-input above; an unrecognized value (e.g. hand-edited) falls back to "small" the same way. A bigger model needs more GPU memory and is slower to load/run — "small" already transcribes English well but noticeably worse on lower-resource languages like Norwegian (see notes.md, "small model quality"); the user is expected to try a bigger size and see what actually fits and helps, not have it decided for them.

key.name: depth-generation-enabled
key.summary: Whether images without a depth map get one generated automatically
key.description: John, 2026-09-30, correcting an earlier misunderstanding: "Vi skal ha en toggle hvor vi slår på depth generation via analyse av bilder... Når vi slår på funksjonaliteten så skal modellen lastes ned. Nedlastingen skal ikke vente til et bilde skal analyseres, vi skal gjøre prefetch" — same shape as transcribe-audio/ diarize-audio above: default off, and turning it on triggers an actual eager model download right then (see start_depth_model_prefetch(), same auto-subprocess-on-toggle pattern as diarize-audio's own start_diarization_model_ prefetch() — no manual terminal step needed here, unlike transcribe-audio's copy-paste dialog, since Depth-Anything-V2 isn't gated and needs no account/token setup first). Off means maybe_generate_depth_on_the_fly() returns immediately for every image, same as transcribe-audio off skips maybe_transcribe_ segment() entirely.

key.name: depth-model-size
key.summary: Which Depth-Anything-V2 model size generate_depth.py loads
key.description: Same shape as transcription-model-size above (John, 2026-09-30: "Vi skal ha samme metodikk for å laste ned modellen for dybdedata. Denne skal også ha valg for model size hvis flere størrelser er tilgjengelig") — they do exist here too, confirmed (not assumed): depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-{Small,Base, Large}-hf are three real, separate HF repos. One of "small" (default)/"base"/"large" — a plain string enum, not a GSettings enum type, same convention as yaw-augmented-input/ transcription-model-size; an unrecognized value falls back to "small" the same way. A bigger model is more accurate but slower and needs more memory — no auto-fit here either (depth generation currently runs on CPU as often as not, see find_device() in generate_depth.py, so this matters even without a GPU involved).

key.name: depth-use-fiducial-markers
key.summary: Whether ArUco markers are used to anchor depth to real-world distance
key.description: John, 2026-09-30: "Vi skal ha et valg for å slå på bruk av referansepunkt. Disse kalles gjerne fiducial markers. Vi bruker ArUco-markører for å beregne avstand og 3D-posisjon (pose estimation)." AprilTag was considered and explicitly set aside for now in favor of ArUco (via OpenCV's own cv2.aruco module, not yet a dependency of demo/depth/requirements.txt) — "da bruker vi aruco, med tilpasningen for AprilTag-familiens ordbøker hvis det blir nødvendig" — cv2.aruco can detect AprilTag-family dictionaries directly if the extra robustness against poor lighting/distance/skewed angle ever turns out to be needed, without a second, more niche dependency. Only meaningful (and only shown in Preferences) while depth-generation-enabled is also on — see notes.md's calibration-marker plan for the wider design this feeds into; the marker-detection/pose- estimation implementation itself doesn't exist yet, this key only carries the on/off intent so far.

key.name: show-depth-at-pointer
key.summary: Whether the "depth: X.XX" readout follows the pointer
key.description: John, 2026-09-24 — a sighted-tester verification aid only (like the gaze cursor), never something a blind end user relies on, so it can be turned off in Preferences for anyone who finds it distracting or is testing without it. Defaults off (John, 2026-09-24): opt-in verification aid, not something that should show up unasked the first time someone opens an equirect image with a depth file.

key.name: prod-cue-duration-ms
key.summary: How long the prod-event visual cue takes to fade out, in milliseconds
key.description: A soft white glow shown briefly at a prod event's position — the demo's mouse click stands in for a real blink-triggered prod (John, 2026-09-30: "Prod evens for eye gaze starter ved blunking, men i demoen så bruker vi klikking med musa som tilnærming... Vi legger på en fuzzy sky der pekeren er"), and the glow is the visible confirmation that it registered. Chosen as a tunable setting rather than a fixed constant, deliberately — John wants to calibrate duration/size/peak-opacity together against real testers until the cue reads as "visible to a sighted tester, not to someone with residual vision," a target no single guessed number can hit outright. See prod-cue-diameter-scale and prod-cue-peak-opacity, which tune the same cue.

key.name: prod-cue-diameter-scale
key.summary: Prod-event glow diameter, as a multiple of the gaze cursor's own diameter
key.description: Relative to gaze_cursor_diameter_px(), not an absolute pixel size, so it scales the same way the gaze cursor itself already does with viewing distance/screen size. See prod-cue-duration-ms's own description for the wider design this is part of.

key.name: prod-cue-peak-opacity
key.summary: Prod-event glow's opacity at its brightest (center, moment it appears)
key.description: The glow is a radial gradient fading to fully transparent at its own edge regardless of this value — this only sets how strong the center itself starts out before the whole thing fades over prod-cue-duration-ms. See prod-cue-duration-ms's own description for the wider design this is part of.

key.name: depth-estimate-grid-size
key.summary: Grid element count for a prod's averaged distance estimate
key.description: John, 2026-09-30, first take on the acoustic model's distance cue: "Når prod'et kommer så beregner vi en midlere avstand innenfor et grid sentrert på det som tilsvarer en gaze-sirkel. Grid'en består av ett element, 4, 9, 16, og 25. Disse grid-størrelsene gjør vi valgbare i Innstillinger." The value is the element count (N×N for N=1..5), matching how John named the options directly, not N itself. See compute_prod_distance_m() (main.cpp) for how the grid itself is laid out and averaged.

key.name: noise-pulse-attack-ms
key.summary: Noise-pulse ADSR attack time, in milliseconds
key.description: First take on the acoustic model's carrier signal (John, 2026-09-30): "Vi skal lage en støypuls. Dette skal ha en klassisk ADSR som parametre... ADSR må antakelig tunes for å få et godt lydbilde" — tunable rather than fixed for exactly that reason. See noise_pulse.hpp/.cpp for the synthesis itself.

key.name: noise-pulse-decay-ms
key.summary: Noise-pulse ADSR decay time, in milliseconds
key.description: See noise-pulse-attack-ms's own description for the wider design this is part of.

key.name: noise-pulse-sustain-level
key.summary: Noise-pulse ADSR sustain level (0-1, not a duration)
key.description: The classic ADSR "S" — a level, not a time (see noise-pulse-sustain-ms for the duration that level is actually held, which classic ADSR doesn't need since it assumes a held/released key; a one-shot prod has no such gesture). See noise-pulse-attack-ms's own description for the wider design.

key.name: noise-pulse-sustain-ms
key.summary: How long the noise-pulse's sustain level is held, in milliseconds
key.description: Not one of the classic four ADSR parameters — added because a prod is a discrete, instantaneous event with no held/released gesture for Sustain to last "as long as" (see noise-pulse-sustain-level's own description). Without this, Release would have no well-defined moment to begin.

key.name: noise-pulse-release-ms
key.summary: Noise-pulse ADSR release time, in milliseconds
key.description: See noise-pulse-attack-ms's own description for the wider design this is part of.

key.name: noise-pulse-color
key.summary: Noise-pulse color/brightness (0 dark .. 1 bright)
key.description: John, 2026-09-30: "Støypulsen skal være farget, så vi trenger en color-parameter. Denne parametren er delvis under brukerens kontrol, men vi skal gjøre ytterligere filtrering" — this is the user-facing half: the target brightness. The code applies the actual one-pole lowpass filter that produces it (the "ytterligere filtrering") — see NoisePulseImpl::render_one_sample() (noise_pulse.cpp). 0 filters heavily (dark/brown noise), 1 barely filters at all (bright/white noise).

key.name: noise-pulse-gain
key.summary: Noise-pulse overall linear amplitude (0-1)
key.description: See noise-pulse-attack-ms's own description for the wider design this is part of.

key.name: noise-pulse-max-delay-ms
key.summary: Ceiling on the distance-based echo delay, in milliseconds
key.description: John, 2026-09-30, first take on the distance→delay mapping ("100 meter er omtrent 0.3 sekund forsinkelse"): a real bug found live the same day — raw_depth_to_distance_m()'s own floor caps distance at 10,000 m for sky/far-background pixels (a reasonable ceiling for the *distance estimate*), which unclamped is up to 30 seconds of delay, enough for a pulse to surface long after anything currently happening, reading as "random prods lenge etter at det burde stoppet... kan se ut som det kommer fra muspekeren." This caps the delay itself, not the distance estimate. See distance_to_delay_ms() (main.cpp).

key.name: noise-pulse-max-delay-is-no-data
key.summary: Whether exceeding the max delay means "no reliable distance" (silent) rather than just capping it
key.description: John, 2026-09-30: "Vi kan bruke en valgfri cap hvor vi setter 'ingen data'" — sky/undefined regions give a raw depth near zero (measured directly: 30-40% of pixels in several real example depth files), which the reciprocal distance formula blows up into an enormous delay rather than a genuinely far-but-real surface ("Det er dybden som går til 10 000 meter! :D"). On (the default): past noise-pulse-max-delay-ms, play nothing at all rather than guess. Off: clamp to the max delay instead, the original behavior. See distance_to_delay_ms() (main.cpp).

key.name: head-prod-sequence-step-ms
key.summary: Delay between steps of a head-prod's elevation sweep, in milliseconds
key.description: A head-prod is a swept sequence of individual prods, not one prod at center (John, 2026-09-30, extending the periscope-graticule head-direction cross: "Når vi utløser en head-prod så er det en sekvens av slike. Vi starter ved -25° og jobber oss oppover til +15°, og fyrer en prod ved hvert 5° merke" — nine steps, -25°/-20°/-15°/-10°/-5°/0°/5°/10°/15°, the same elevations the graticule's own ticks and top endpoint mark). This is the delay between each step; 0 fires the whole sequence back-to-back with no visible sweep at all. Default guessed at 50ms (John: "Jeg tror default er rundt 50ms, men jeg vet ikke. Kan være helt ned i 20ms") — tunable rather than fixed, same "calibrate live" reasoning as prod-cue-duration-ms and friends.

key.name: last-project
key.summary: Last opened/created project directory
key.description: John, 2026-10-xx: a project is a directory holding a protocol.md plus its related recording sessions — reopened automatically on next launch, same "remember the working context" convention as current-working-session. Empty string means none yet.

key.name: recent-projects
key.summary: Recently opened/created project directories
key.description: Absolute directory paths, most recent first — the new project dropdown's own recents list, leftmost in the header bar.

key.name: max-recent-projects
key.summary: Maximum number of recent projects to remember
key.description: Caps the project dropdown's recents list — older entries are dropped once a new project is opened past this count.

key.name: project-slug-counter
key.summary: Global counter used to make new project directory names unique
key.description: John, 2026-10-xx: "tror vi legger til et tall fra gsettings for å unngå kollisjoner. Dette tallet inkrementerer vi hver gang vi tar et nytt i bruk." Incremented every time a new project directory is actually created (including retries after an on-disk name collision) — never decremented, and never guaranteed consistent with another app/machine sharing the same parent directory. No Preferences row — this is bookkeeping, not a user-facing option; edit it directly in gsettings if ever needed.

key.name: project-slug-counter-digits
key.summary: Zero-padded digit count for the project directory counter
key.description: John, 2026-10-xx: "bruker 6 tall (?) og fyller inn null'er for å gjøre det mer lesbart." No Preferences row — read straight from gsettings, same "no UI, edit the key directly if needed" convention as max-recent-projects' own undecorated siblings.

key.name: project-title-cutoff-chars
key.summary: Max characters shown on the project dropdown's own button face
key.description: John, 2026-10-xx: "Venstre side i dropdown'en skal vise navnet på prosjektet... med en cut-off og hellip om den er for lang. Antall tegn går i gsettings... brukeren kan endre verdien rett i gsettings om nødvendig." No Preferences row by design.

key.name: session-title-cutoff-chars
key.summary: Max characters shown on the session dropdown's own button face
key.description: John, 2026-10-03: "Og så må dette venstrefeltet ha en maks lengde, som hentes fra gsettings. Ved overflow så legges det på en hellip" — the session dropdown's button face shows "[creator]: [contributor]" (session_button_label(), main.cpp), truncated the same way project-title-cutoff-chars truncates the project dropdown's own label. No Preferences row by design, same convention as project-title-cutoff-chars.

key.name: image-title-cutoff-chars
key.summary: Max characters shown on the image dropdown's own button face
key.description: John, 2026-10-06: image titles had no cutoff at all until now, unlike project-title-cutoff-chars/session-title-cutoff-chars — an uncapped title's own varying width was part of why clicking Previous/Next shifted those buttons right out from under the user's next click ("da kan brukeren klikke feil"). Same truncate-then-ellipsis convention as the other two. No Preferences row by design, same convention as those.

key.name: last-project-parent-folder
key.summary: Last parent folder used when creating/opening a project
key.description: Same "remember the last folder" convention as last-image-folder, for the New/Open Project folder pickers.

key.name: preferred-bigrams
key.summary: Pinned name-to-bigram mappings for the monitoring matrix's header buttons
key.description: John, 2026-10-12: assign_bigrams() (monitoring_dialogs.cpp) otherwise picks a participant's two-letter header label fresh every session from their name alone, which can land on a different pair session to session. A name present here gets its mapped bigram instead, honored unless it collides with an earlier participant's own pinned or natural choice. Normally holds only a couple of entries — typically just the user's own full name, so their own header stays recognizable across sessions. Edited via the Preferences dialog.

key.name: preferred-sink-devices
key.summary: Preferred listening device per fixed participant
key.description: John, 2026-10-12: a default for MonitoringState:: sink_device_assignment (monitoring.hpp) — Ambient Speaker and every name with a preferred bigram (the same "fixed participants" set as preferred-bigrams). Each value is "device id\x1Fdisplay name" (preferences.cpp's own encode/ decode_preferred_device()) — a nested a{s(ss)} dict-of-tuples was tried first and didn't round-trip through glibmm's generic map-to-Variant template (cast_dynamic() threw std::bad_cast reading it back, crashing the app), so this stays on the same flat a{ss} shape preferred-bigrams already proved works. Only seeded into a session's actual state when no assignment already exists there (seed_preferred_devices(), monitoring_dialogs.cpp) — a default, not a lock, so it's freely overridden per session; what actually gets logged to a track is always that live state, never this setting directly. An empty device id means "no preferred device, assign it by hand each session" instead. Edited via the Preferences dialog.

key.name: preferred-source-devices
key.summary: Preferred microphone device per fixed participant
key.description: Same shape and seeding rule as preferred-sink-devices, for MonitoringState::source_device_assignment — Ambient Microphone and every name with a preferred bigram.

key.name: synthesized-volumes
key.summary: Synthesized volume per listener
key.description: Keyed by participant name, or by the Ambient Speaker's sentinel id. Set on the synthesized sound played into that listener's own output device; the device's own volume is never changed. Participants on the Ambient Speaker have none of their own. In dB; no entry means 0 dB.

key.name: participants-volumes
key.summary: Participants volume per listener

key.name: pointer-fixation-ms
key.summary: Pointer fixation time (ms)
key.description: How long the mouse pointer, standing in for an eye tracker, must rest before it prods where it stopped (an implicit eye-prod). Also how recent head movement must be for such a pause to count as head tracking rather than a gaze shift. Suited to a mouse only; a real eye tracker's fixations are much shorter and need their own value.

key.name: agc-target-dbfs
key.summary: Voice levelling target (dBFS)
key.description: RMS speech level the voice leveller aims for, shared by every microphone. -23 dBFS matches EBU R 128's -23 LUFS loudness target closely enough for speech.

key.name: agc-attack-ms
key.summary: Voice levelling attack (ms)
key.description: How quickly the leveller turns a loud speaker down.

key.name: agc-release-ms
key.summary: Voice levelling release (ms)
key.description: How quickly the leveller turns a quiet speaker up.

key.name: agc-max-gain-db
key.summary: Voice levelling maximum gain (dB)
key.description: The most the leveller raises or lowers a speaker. Kept moderate so a quiet microphone's room noise is never lifted far.

key.name: source-agc
key.summary: Voice levelling on/off per participant
key.description: Keyed like source-volumes. No entry means on.

key.name: source-volumes
key.summary: Voice volume per participant
key.description: Keyed by participant name, or by the Ambient Microphone's sentinel id. Applied to what every listener hears from that microphone, not to the microphone itself, so recordings stay untouched. In dB; no entry means 0 dB.
